newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China protests against Manila move on Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: China protests against Manila move on Spratlys.

text.p: China has protested against the opening of an airstrip on one of the disputed South China Sea Spratly Islands by the Philippines armed forces' chief.

"China enjoys indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha (Spratly) Islands and the adjacent water," the Chinese Embassy said in a statement received here on Monday. "China hopes that the Philippines side could...refrain from any move to harm friendly international relations."
Philippines military chief General Arnulfo Acedera inaugurated the airstrip on the Kalayaan island group on December 25.

Manila claims ownership of the eight-island Kalayaan group in the Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich but largely uninhabited isles, shoals and reefs claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.

Tension between the Philippines and China flared in the area last year when Manila accused the Chinese of building what it said were possible naval structures on Mischief Reef, which Manila says is part of Kalayaan.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Philippine President Fidel Ramos agreed during Jiang's visit to Manila last month to shelve differences over the Spratlys and consider cooperation in developing the area.
